sections.h2: What should I know first about selling a house in Roseville, Michigan?
sections.html:
Roseville is a compact, densely built Macomb County city, and the clearest local rule for sellers concerns rental houses: a registered rental carries a city Certificate of Compliance and an ownership transfer fee. For any house, the rest of the process runs through the Macomb County Register of Deeds and the city assessor.

The city lies in southern Macomb County, roughly 13 to 14 miles northeast of downtown Detroit. It became a village in 1926 and a city in 1958, when the village and the rest of Erin Township merged. A population that tripled between 1950 and 1960 suggests that much of the housing stock dates from that era, so a pre-listing walk-through helps you see what a buyer's inspector will find.

Below you will find the population history, the Census housing figures, the roads and schools buyers ask about, and the exact fees and dates that apply when a Roseville house changes hands.

sections.h2: How has Roseville's population changed over the decades?
sections.html:
Roseville grew very quickly in the 1950s, then slowly shrank. The count rose from 15,816 in 1950 to 50,195 in 1960 and peaked at 60,529 in 1970, and it has stayed between 47,000 and 55,000 since 1980.

The latest estimate, for July 1, 2025, is 46,863, which is 1.8 percent below the 2020 base. In practical terms Roseville has a large stock of single-family houses built for a bigger population, and it has about 4,850 people per square mile of land.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Roseville homes?
sections.html:
For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau lists a median value of $155,800 for owner-occupied homes in Roseville, with 65.6 percent of homes owner-occupied. A buyer's monthly cost with a mortgage is a median $1,246, and a house without a mortgage runs $536 a month in owner costs.

  • Median gross rent is $1,233, close to the median owner cost with a mortgage.
  • There are 21,226 households with a median income of $62,182 and 2.21 people each.
  • About 90.8 percent of residents lived in the same house one year earlier.
  • Roughly 15.5 percent of adults 25 and older have a bachelor's degree, and 12.5 percent of residents are below the poverty line.

Price your house against recent Roseville sales rather than county averages, and ask your agent or title company for the sold prices on your own street before you set a number.

sections.h2: Which roads, neighbors and schools do Roseville buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Roseville is crossed by two freeways and two state routes, which makes it an easy base for commuters. I-696, the Walter P. Reuther Freeway, runs east to west through the middle of the city. I-94 forms part of the eastern boundary with St. Clair Shores. M-3, which is Gratiot Avenue, roughly bisects the city on its way from Detroit to Mount Clemens, and M-97, Groesbeck Highway, is near the western edge. The mean commute is 25.7 minutes.

The city borders St. Clair Shores to the east, Eastpointe to the south, Warren to the west, and Fraser and Clinton Township to the north. Mount Clemens, the Macomb County seat, is about 7 miles northeast.

Two districts teach Roseville children. Roseville Community Schools run seven elementary schools, two middle schools and one high school, and Fraser Public Schools runs two elementary schools inside the city. The charter school Conner Creek Academy East is also in the city. Macomb Mall, which opened in 1964 west of Gratiot, remains an anchor for shopping.

sections.h2: What rules apply if the Roseville house is a rental?
sections.html:
Roseville regulates non-owner-occupied housing under its Non-Owner Occupied Housing Ordinance, and a rental that passes inspection receives a Certificate of Compliance. After an application and payment, the rental division contacts the owner to schedule an inspection.

  • Initial inspection and first reinspection: $150 for a single family house or duplex, $100 for apartments and condominiums.
  • Each additional unit at the same location, registered with the first: $50.
  • Lockout fee: $25.
  • Transfer of ownership: $25 for the first unit and $10 for each additional unit.

The city charges that ownership transfer fee on registered rentals, so ask the rental division who files the update and when. Give a buyer who plans to keep tenants your most recent Certificate of Compliance. You can reach the rental division at rentals@roseville-mi.gov, and it can tell you whether your address still needs a registration after the sale.

sections.h2: What does the buyer file with the Roseville assessor?
sections.html:
The buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit with the assessor within 45 days of closing, and a late filing costs $5 a day up to $200. The city's assessor also notes the buyer signs the Principal Residence Exemption form at closing, which exempts 18 mills of school operating tax.

As the seller, sign the Request to Rescind Principal Residence form and file it with the Assessing Office. That removes your name from the homestead and lets you claim the exemption on your next home. Every May the assessing staff inspects properties that sold or have active building permits, in preparation for the next year's roll.

Roseville sets assessed value at 50 percent of fair market value, and taxable value rises each year by inflation or 5 percent, whichever is less, except after a transfer of ownership or a physical change. Residential owners who want to appeal must do so by appointment or in writing before the March Board of Review closes. A hardship exemption can be requested at the March, July or December boards.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a Roseville deed in Macomb County?
sections.html:
Macomb County records every document for a flat $30, no matter the page count, and adds $3 for each extra instrument that a document assigns or discharges. Of that $30, $4 goes into the state survey and remonumentation fund.

Warranty deeds and land contracts need a tax certificate from the county treasurer first. The fee is $5 for up to five legal descriptions and $0.20 for each additional one. The Register of Deeds is at 120 N. Main St. in Mount Clemens.

Macomb's schedule shows state transfer tax at $3.75 per $500 and county transfer tax at $0.55 per $500, or the sale price times 0.0075 for the state and times 0.0011 for the county. The seller pays. Exemptions listed by the county include conveyances from an individual to a child or grandchild, transfers in foreclosure and instruments under $100. The exemption must be cited on the deed, so give your title agent the facts early.

sections.h2: When are Roseville property taxes due, and what if they are late?
sections.html:
Roseville mails summer bills in July and winter bills in December. Summer taxes are due August 31, with a penalty of 1 percent a month starting September 1, and winter taxes are due February 28. On March 1 every unpaid balance goes to the Macomb County Treasurer.

Seniors age 62 or older with household income under $40,000 can ask the treasurer to defer the summer due date to February 28, with 1 percent monthly interest. The deferment form must be filed by September 15. The Treasurer's Office also helps senior homeowners and renters file their state homestead credits for free.

Duplicate bills cost $2 per parcel. If you are selling in the weeks after a due date, ask the title company to confirm payment before closing so the buyer does not inherit a penalty.

faqs.q: Does Roseville charge a fee to transfer a rental to a new owner?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's rental fee schedule lists $25 for the first unit and $10 for each additional unit when ownership transfers.

faqs.q: How much does Macomb County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: $30 per document regardless of pages, with $4 of that sent to the state survey fund. A warranty deed also needs a $5 tax certificate for up to five legal descriptions.

faqs.q: When are the two Roseville tax bills due?
faqs.a: August 31 for summer and February 28 for winter. Unpaid taxes go to the Macomb County Treasurer on March 1.

faqs.q: Who pays Michigan transfer tax on a Roseville sale?
faqs.a: The seller. Macomb's schedule applies 0.0075 of the price for the state tax and 0.0011 for the county tax.

faqs.q: What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: Sign and file the city's Request to Rescind Principal Residence form so your name comes off the old homestead. Then apply for the exemption on your new home.
